title: Stability Scenario Activation Lattice
body:
One-line purpose: a compact, phase-aware KPI and contingency tracker to drive safe traffic activation and rapid remediation during early production ramps.

Scope: launches with staged traffic (alpha -> beta -> staged -> GA) where the primary risk vector is request-level error rate, latency tail, and cost per 1k tokens. This sheet is intended to be the single operational source-of-truth for the first 14 days of ramp.

Key SLOs (operational):
- P95 latency <= configured latency SLO per model variant
- 5xx rate < 0.25% (critical), < 1.0% (warning)
- Error budget spend <= 20% per day during ramp window
- Cost per 1k tokens within +/- 15% of forecast

KPI columns (sheet view): Phase | Date range | Traffic % target | P95 latency (ms) | 5xx % | Avg tokens/req | Cost/1k | Ramp owner | Mitigation tier | Gate decision (go/hold/rollback) | Notes

Phases and gating criteria (example rows):
- Alpha (0-1%): gate = manual. Proceed if 5xx < 1.0% AND P95 < SLO*1.3. If fail -> ticket infra+runtime, hold gateway, run canary diagnostics.
- Beta (1-10%): gate = ops-approved. Proceed if 5xx < 0.5% AND P95 < SLO*1.15 AND cost drift < 25%. If fail -> scale dedicated capacity OR switch to compatible quantized model variant.
- Staged (10-50%): gate = automated (slo checks + oncall ack). Proceed if 5xx < 0.25% AND P95 < SLO. If fail -> auto-fallback to stable model variant and route traffic to secondary region.
- GA (>50%): gate = product ops + eng sign-off. Proceed if historical 14-day rolling metrics within thresholds.

Contingency actions (tiered):
- Tier A (critical): immediate rollback of rollout percentage by 80%, re-route to fallback model/region, hotfix patch or config revert, pager to SRE + runtime team.
- Tier B (degradation): throttle non-critical routes, increase autoscaling buffer, enable KV cache warmup, schedule next-available deploy window for fix.
- Tier C (cost/quality drift): enable cost-saver config (batching up, quantize variant), notify finance and product, run prompt-quality smoke tests.

Runbook snippets (notes-to-self style):
- Diagnostic checklist: collect tail traces, top 10 failing request examples, model variant diff (weights/quantization), GPU memory pressure, kernel/driver logs, network spikes.
- Quick rollback command: infra rollback --deployment <id> --percent -80 (ops playbook link in linked_artifacts).
- Canary probes: synthetic user journeys (3 types) every 60s; store last 100 probes in metrics bucket for triage.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Finalize SLO numeric values per model family (Rhea to own).
- Add cost attribution tag to every test traffic batch (Marcus).
- Automate gate decision dashboard (depend on INFRA-1297).

Sign-off matrix (required before GA):
- Product ops: readiness ok (name)
- Serving runtime: performance ok (name)
- Infra/SRE: capacity & failover ok (name)
- Security/Compliance: data handling ok (name)

Notes on usage: keep this sheet lightweight—link to deep-dive runbooks instead of duplicating content. When copying for a new launch, update the model SLO row and the linked artifacts.

Last adoption reminder: during the first 48 hours of ramp, reduce scheduled deployments across related services and keep a one-hour change freeze window unless emergency fix.
